text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty page triggered for service `inference-api-eu` (pd-12345). Symptoms: sustained 5xx spike (~12% error rate over 2m), elevated latency. Link: https://pagerduty.com/incidents/pd-12345

alex (oncall): ack — i'm oncall, taking ownership. starting triage. any idea whether this is region-only?

jamie (sre): on it, pulling metrics from grafana. seeing error increase around LB -> inference-svc. looks like 502/504 downstream errors.

ryan (eng): flagged a new deploy ~10m ago? @alex did we roll a new model/weights to eu pool?

alex (oncall): not from my side. I see a canary earlier. checking deploy history...

alex (oncall): starting a quick bridge — joining zoom  https://zoom.us/j/xxxxx (reacted :eyes:)

jamie (sre): running quick logs and tail. ssh to pod and tail:
```
kubectl -n inference logs -l app=inference-api -c runtime --since=5m | grep ERROR | tail -n 50
```

jamie (sre): stack trace shows kv-cache lookup timeouts and repeated "KVCache: shard unavailable" errors.

ryan (eng): that smells like redis/etcd/kv service issue. can someone check kv-cache cluster health? `kvctl status`?

alex (oncall): matt (infra) notified via PD escalation. @ryan can you validate recent config changes to kv-cache? if not, i'll trigger fallback to local-prefix-cache.

ryan (eng): looking now. I didn't touch kv configs. checking autoscaler: pods are healthy but latency to kv nodes from eu-inference nodes high (~400ms).

maya (customer-success): heads up — i started a quick customer ping list for EU paying customers. so far two support tickets from Acme and BrightApps reporting failures.

alex (oncall): customer impact: transient failures for some EU customers; rate-limited retries will likely surface as increased latency. severity: P2 -> P1 if more customers.

jamie (sre): mitigation attempt: triggering kv-cache fallback on 2 nodes in eu pool:
```
kubectl -n inference patch deployment inference-api -p '{"spec":{"template":{"metadata":{"annotations":{"kv-cache-mode":"local-fallback"}}}}}'
```

alex (oncall): do it, jamie. i'll monitor error rate.

jamie (sre): applied to one AZ — errors dropped from 12% -> 3% in ~90s. pushing to remaining AZs.

ryan (eng): good signal. while that stabilizes, i'm investigating network path to kv nodes and opening a ticket with infra.

maya (customer-success): sending templated notice to impacted customers now. cc ops for status updates.

alex (oncall): handing ownership to jamie for post-mitigation follow-up. i'm stepping off but reachable if it resurfaces. please post root cause hypothesis and next steps.

jamie (sre): taking over. current status: reduced error rate, stabilizing. next steps: validate kv cluster health, run full post-incident runbook, plan for durable fallback config and alerts.

ryan (eng): i'll pair with infra to validate network flaps and any config drift. will add rollback of recent canary if we find correlation.

maya (customer-success): i'll update the tickets with mitigation status and ETA for follow-up.

alex (oncall): thanks all. tagging postmortem owners: jamie (lead), ryan (network), maya (customer comms). (reacted :thumbsup:)

incident-bot: Incident pd-12345 status changed: acknowledged by alex (oncall).
